body.title: The lotus across traditions
body.summary: A shared symbol can carry different meanings across religious, artistic and historical contexts.

rationale.text: The lotus plays a central role in the art of several Indian religions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Sikhism and Jainism. The lotus throne — a stylised flower used as a seat or base — is the normal pedestal for divine figures in Buddhist and Hindu art.
Within each tradition the image is read in its own way. Hindu deities such as Vishnu and Lakshmi are often shown on a lotus; in a Pali text the Buddha compares himself to a lotus.

whyItMatters.text: Following one image across traditions helps explain why similar-looking art can mean different things, and why context — the figure, the text, the period — matters when reading it.

body.doesNotEstablish: Similar imagery does not prove a single shared origin, a direct line of influence, or identical meaning. The sources here describe how the lotus is used, not how the motif travelled between traditions.
body.uncertainty: Interpretations of the lotus's meaning vary within each tradition, not only between them.
